minutes.headline: ZBA heard a bid to split a Laurel Lane lot into two 50-ft-frontage lots and continued it to December 13 without ruling.
minutes.summary: The board heard a special permit application from the owners of 100 Laurel Lane, presented by their son, to split a lot with 100 ft of frontage into two lots with 50 ft each. Several members said it is really a variance with a very high bar, and raised driveway, easement and private-road problems. To avoid a denial that would bar a return for two years, the applicant agreed to a continuance so he can consult the Planning Board.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued the 100 Laurel Lane special permit hearing to December 13 by vote, without ruling on it.
The application would split one lot into two lots with equal, reduced frontage; several members said it amounts to a variance, which carries a very high bar.
Members raised problems with driveways, an easement, a private road and the lot's frontage and width.
The applicant will speak with the Planning Board and may submit new information when the hearing resumes.
The board explained that a continuance resumes the hearing where it stands, while a withdrawal would start a new hearing.

why_it_matters: A proposal to divide one residential lot into two reduced-frontage lots on a private road is being tested against the town's frontage rules, and the outcome could serve as a precedent for similar requests in nearby neighborhoods.
